newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET STILL LIQUID, RATES MIXED.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET STILL LIQUID, RATES MIXED.

text.p: Short term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed on Wednesday as the market continued flush with cash on the back of maturing paper, dealers said.
"The market opened in surplus today and we're expecting an extra Z$746 million in maturities," a dealer said.
He added that there was a high demand for treasury bills which most players were looking to sell for a profit at lower rates after Thursday's weekly auction.
Meanwhile on Thursday, discount houses were taking up the central bank paper at a stable 21.46 percent but were selling it marginally firmer at 21.35 percent from Tuesday's 21.25 percent.

NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold softer at 23 and 22 percent respectively from 23.25 and 22.50 percent but bankers acceptances were quoted unchanged at 21.75 and 21.50 percent.
Call money was also steady at 23 percent with the central Reserve Bank indicating a market surplus of Z$120 million at the opening, slightly up from Tuesday's Z$101 million.
